title: E. Prefix GCD
statement:
Since Mansur is tired of making legends, there will be no legends for this task.

You are given an array of positive integer numbers a_1, a_2, …, a_n. The elements of the array can be rearranged in any order. You need to find the smallest possible value of the expression gcd(a_1) + gcd(a_1, a_2) + … + gcd(a_1, a_2, …, a_n), where gcd(a_1, a_2, …, a_n) denotes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of a_1, a_2, …, a_n.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single number n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) — the size of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n numbers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^5) — the initial array.

The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

The sum of max(a_1, a_2, …, a_n) over all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

For each test case, output a single number on a separate line — the answer to the problem.

In the first test case, the elements can be rearranged as follows: [2, 4, 2]. Then the answer will be gcd(2) + gcd(2, 4) + gcd(2, 4, 2) = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

In the third test case, the elements can be rearranged as follows: [6, 10, 15]. Then the answer will be gcd(6) + gcd(6, 10) + gcd(6, 10, 15) = 6 + 2 + 1 = 9.

Input:
```
534 2 226 3310 15 656 42 12 52 20442 154 231 66
```

Output:
```
6
6
9
14
51
```
